passage: The power cut at six meant no fan, and the room Lavanya shared with her younger brother Anirban was hot and loud. Board exams were five months away, and Lavanya was tired of that feeling of not knowing what to study next. With a ruler and a marker she drew a chart on the back of an old calendar: seven to seven-forty, maths; then a short break; then science, another break, then social studies. She taped it to the wall above the study table. When the lights came back she started the first block. Anirban read the chart and asked, "Where's my slot?" Lavanya laughed and wrote his drawing time in blue, beside hers.

qa.a: Lavanya taped it to the wall above the study table.

qa.a: Lavanya was tired of not knowing what to study next, and probably anxious about the board exams five months away.

qa.a: Lavanya could lengthen that block on the chart after noticing it, or add a second block for it on another day, so the plan fits what really happens.

qa.q: How might Anirban have felt about the chart?
qa.a: Anirban may have felt left out at first, as his question shows, and then included once his drawing time went up beside hers.

passage:
Board exams were four months away, and Ira kept doing whatever subject felt urgent that evening, usually maths, never social science.
On Sunday she took a chart paper and a ruler into the living room of their Jaipur flat. Her friend Alka, visiting, helped her draw it.
Five in the evening to nine-thirty, split into forty-minute blocks. After each block, ten minutes' break. Monday: maths, science, English, social science. Tuesday: science, Hindi, maths, social science. Each subject coloured differently.
"Why forty minutes?" Alka asked.
"After forty I start staring at the ceiling," Ira said.
She taped the chart above her desk. On Monday at 5.40, the maths block ended. She got up, drank water and switched to science, even though she was in the middle of a chapter.
By Friday, social science had five blocks. Last month, it had none.

qa.q: How long was each study block?
qa.a: Each study block was forty minutes.

qa.q: How might Ira have felt switching to science in the middle of a chapter?
qa.a: She may have felt a little reluctant to stop, but also relieved that each subject would get its fair turn.

qa.q: What else could Ira add to her chart, and why?
qa.a: She could add a small tick for each block completed, so she can see at a glance which subjects are getting their time.

qa.q: How might Alka see Ira's timetable?
qa.a: Alka is curious about the forty minutes and may find the idea useful for her own study after hearing Ira's reason.

grounding: It shows a Class 10 student dividing evenings into forty-minute subject blocks with breaks, and marking them on a wall chart.

"What's that?" Anirban asked, pointing at the chart on the wall.
"My timetable," Omkar said. "Class 10 boards are in March. I kept starting maths at six and still doing maths at ten."
"So what did you change?"
"Look. Every evening is five blocks of forty minutes. Ten-minute break after each. Maths, science, English, social, Hindi, rotating so each gets four blocks a week at least."
"And if you're in the middle of something when the forty minutes end?"
"I mark where I stopped and move on. It comes back in the next maths block."
Anirban traced the colours with his finger. "Social science is on here more than maths."
"Because I kept skipping it. Now it has its own boxes, so I can't."
"Can you make me one?"
Omkar laughed and handed him a blank chart paper. "Make your own. That's half the point."

qa.q: When does Omkar take the ten-minute break?
qa.a: The ten-minute break comes after each block of forty minutes.

qa.q: How does Omkar seem to feel about the new timetable?
qa.a: Omkar seems confident and relieved, since subjects he used to skip now have their own boxes.

qa.q: What else could Omkar do after a few weeks with the chart?
qa.a: He could check which blocks he keeps missing and adjust them, so the chart fits how his evenings really go.

qa.q: How might Anirban see Omkar's chart?
qa.a: Anirban is impressed and wants one too, though Omkar tells him to make his own.
